annotations.text:
COMPACTED

No thumbnail, so the name starts at the edge and the price sits beside it. The name itself is the link to the tea, and Remove sits at the far end of the amount label, so the block spends no row on chrome.

Each block is washed in the colour its tea brews, the same left-to-right ground a shop row carries, so the type reads at a glance without a swatch to look at.

A hairline under the label separates what the control is called from the amounts themselves, and the total is one line: the word, what the basket holds, the figure.

THE RATE IS THE MECHANIC

Every line carries a flat handling amount that a whole pressed piece skips, so what a gram costs falls as the amount rises. The panel used to print the shelf rate, a figure that never moved while the weights beside it did.

Quoted a gram, because the buttons beside it are grams, and rounded to the nearest cent and no finer: IDR 10.4k down to 9.2k across the ladder, or $0.64 to $0.57, NT$21 to NT$18.

The currency is a control with a border and a chevron, and the type across all three steps went up two or three steps of the scale to be readable on a phone held at arm's length.

The amounts are the shop's own ladder now, read from the same function the product page calls, so the two cannot drift again. The whole pressed piece joins the row on a tea that has one, and it is the best rate on the row because it skips the handling entirely.
